__comment: Shared byte-for-byte corpus for photo (OCR) ingredient analysis in veganAndroid and veganIOS. Any change must be applied identically in both repositories. Statuses: notVegan | vegan | review. Reason sources: photoAnimalIngredient | photoAnimalAdditive | photoAllPlantRecognized | photoUnrecognizedIngredient.

cases.rationale: A common Spanish label whose every segment is recognised plant or neutral must be the only way to reach a vegan verdict from a photo.
cases.text: Ingredientes: harina de trigo, azúcar, aceite de girasol, sal, levadura.

cases.rationale: The same label in English must give the identical verdict, so the lexicon cannot be Spanish-only.
cases.text: Ingredients: wheat flour, sugar, sunflower oil, salt, yeast.

cases.rationale: OCR keeps percentages, quantities and the heading; none of them is an ingredient and none may push the verdict to review.
cases.text: INGREDIENTES: Tomate (85%), agua, sal 1,2%, aceite de oliva virgen extra (2 %).

cases.rationale: An unambiguous animal ingredient read from the photo condemns the verdict and is reported as the culprit.
cases.text: Ingredientes: harina de trigo, azúcar, mantequilla, huevo.

cases.rationale: German labels are the reported case that motivated this feature; whey must be caught there too.
cases.text: Zutaten: Weizenmehl, Zucker, Molkenpulver, Salz.

cases.rationale: A plant qualifier next to an ambiguous animal word (coconut milk) must not condemn, and must not fall into review either.
cases.text: Ingredients: water, coconut milk, sugar, sea salt.

cases.rationale: An additive of clearly animal origin read as a code condemns the verdict, matching the barcode path.
cases.text: Ingredientes: azúcar, agua, colorante E120, acidulante E330.

cases.rationale: An additive of uncertain origin is not proof of an animal origin, so it must leave the verdict in review rather than condemning it.
cases.text: Ingredientes: harina de trigo, azúcar, emulgente E471, sal.

cases.rationale: An ingredient the lexicon does not know must never be assumed vegan; it is listed so the user can check that one word.
cases.text: Ingredientes: harina de trigo, azúcar, aroma natural, sal.

cases.rationale: When the photo contains both an animal ingredient and an unknown word, the animal ingredient decides; review would understate it.
cases.text: Ingredientes: harina de trigo, gelatina, aroma natural.

cases.rationale: A may-contain warning is cross-contamination guidance about the factory, not an ingredient, so it is surfaced as a note without changing the verdict.
cases.text: Ingredientes: harina de trigo, azúcar, aceite de girasol. Puede contener trazas de leche.

cases.rationale: The trace warning must not hide a real animal ingredient listed before it.
cases.text: Ingredients: wheat flour, honey, sugar. May contain traces of nuts.

cases.rationale: A photo that yielded nothing readable must be review, never vegan.
If the OCR only caught the heading, there is no ingredient evidence at all and the verdict cannot be vegan.
cases.text: INGREDIENTES:

cases.rationale: OCR breaks lines mid-list; newlines must split segments like commas so a wrapped ingredient is still recognised.
cases.text:
Ingredientes: harina
de trigo, azúcar,
sal

cases.rationale: Sub-ingredients in parentheses are real ingredients and must be analysed, not skipped.
cases.text: Ingredientes: chocolate (pasta de cacao, azúcar, manteca de cacao), harina de trigo.

cases.rationale: An animal sub-ingredient hidden inside parentheses must condemn just like a top-level one.
cases.text: Ingredientes: chocolate (pasta de cacao, azúcar, leche en polvo), harina de trigo.

cases.rationale: A function descriptor says what the additive does, not where it comes from, so on its own it is not evidence of a plant origin and must not produce a vegan verdict.
cases.text: Ingredientes: azúcar, agua, colorante natural.

cases.rationale: Same rule for a bare descriptor with no qualifier at all: unknown origin means review, never vegan.
cases.text: Ingredientes: harina de trigo, azúcar, conservante.

cases.rationale: A descriptor qualified by a recognised plant source is legitimate evidence and must not be dragged into review.
cases.text: Ingredientes: chocolate, emulgente lecitina de soja, azúcar.

cases.rationale: Everyday additives written as words instead of E numbers are not animal-derived, and sending a whole label to review because of them would make the feature useless.
cases.text: Ingredientes: harina de trigo, azúcar, maltodextrina, bicarbonato sódico, ácido cítrico.

cases.rationale: Mono and diglycerides may come from animal fat, so the name alone must leave the verdict in review, exactly like the barcode path treats the equivalent additive.
cases.text: Ingredientes: harina de trigo, azúcar, mono y diglicéridos de ácidos grasos.

unrecognized: Mono Y Diglicéridos De Ácidos Grasos

cases.rationale: Glycerin can be of animal or plant origin, so it must never be whitelisted as a recognised plant source.
cases.text: Ingredients: wheat flour, sugar, glycerin.

cases.rationale: OCR loses accents and case; recognition must not depend on either.
cases.text: INGREDIENTES: HARINA DE TRIGO, AZUCAR, ACEITE DE GIRASOL, SAL
